A_target.statement:
Let $D: \mathbf J \to \mathbf C$ be a [[Definition:Diagram (Category Theory)|diagram]].
A [[Definition:Colimit|colimit]] of $D$ is an [[Definition:Initial Object|initial object]] in the [[Definition:Category of Cocones|category of cocones]] under $D$.

B_source.statement:
Let $D: \mathbf J \to \mathbf C$ be a [[Definition:Diagram (Category Theory)|diagram]].
A [[Definition:Limit (Category Theory)|limit]] of $D$ is a [[Definition:Terminal Object|terminal object]] in the [[Definition:Category of Cones|category of cones]] over $D$.

object_map.reformulation: Pass to C^op; the diagram dualizes, cones become cocones, terminal becomes initial.

validity_conditions: Limits and colimits are defined by universal properties stated entirely in terms of arrows.
Reversing all arrows (C -> C^op) sends the limit universal property to the colimit one.
Op is involutive, so colimit in C = limit in C^op.
proof_plan: Express the [[Definition:Limit (Category Theory)|limit]] as a terminal cone, using only morphisms and commuting triangles.

Pass to $\mathbf C^{\text {op} }$, reversing all morphisms.
Cones over $D$ become cocones under $D^{\text {op} }$, and terminal becomes initial.
The dual statement is the definition of the [[Definition:Colimit|colimit]].

Hence a colimit of $D$ in $\mathbf C$ is a limit of $D^{\text {op} }$ in $\mathbf C^{\text {op} }$, and limits and colimits are [[Definition:Dual Statement (Category Theory)|dual]].
{{qed}}
